title: Investigating the material basis and molecular mechanisms underlying the enhanced anti-inflammatory efficacy of ginger-processed anemarrhenae rhizoma via the NF-kappaB/COX-2 pathway.
authors: Ya-Zhu, Wang; Jia-Li, Tian; Xiao-Ting, Wang; Shu-Qing, Tian; Nan, Xu; Hui, Gao
journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis
one_liner_zh: 该研究分析姜制知母化学成分变化并通过分子对接预测其与NF-kappaB/COX-2的结合，但核心是中药抗炎机制，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法。
abstract: This study aims to analyze the differences in chemical constituents before and after the ginger-processing of Anemarrhenae Rhizoma(AR), screen for key differential components, and elucidate their anti-inflammatory mechanisms. Furthermore, it seeks to clarify the principles of processing and the scientific rationale behind the synergistic enhancement achieved through ginger processing. This research provides scientific support for the preservation of traditional processing techniques and the rational clinical application of ginger-processed Anemarrhenae Rhizoma (GAR). The Ultra Performance Liquid Chromatography-Quadrupole-Time of Flight-Tandem Mass Spectrometry (UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS) technology was employed for qualitative analysis of the chemical constituents present in AR and GAR in both positive and negative ion modes. By comparing the variations in constituent levels before and after ginger-processing, as well as identifying newly emerged characteristic peaks, we prioritized novel and upregulated differential components with well-documented pharmacological activities as target compounds. The key differential components were subsequently validated quantitatively using High Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) technology. Furthermore, molecular docking technology was employed to predict the binding affinity of these key differential components with nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NF-kappaB) and cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) proteins. An inflammatory model was established utilizing lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced RAW264.7 macrophages, and the CCK-8 (Cell Counting Kit-8) assay was performed to determine the optimal concentrations of the key differential components and LPS. The levels of tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha) and interleukin-6 (IL-6) in cell supernatants were measured using ELISA, while the expression levels of IkappaBalpha (Inhibitor of nuclear factor kappa B alpha), NF-kappaB, phosphorylated nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (p-NF-kappaB), nuclear NF-kappaB, and COX-2 proteins were assessed through Western blot (WB) analysis. UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS analysis identified 40 compounds in both AR and GAR under both positive and negative ion modes, predominantly comprising saponins. Key differential components (mangiferin, timosaponin BⅡ, 6-gingerol) were screened based on changes in the chemical profile before and after ginger-processing, as well as pharmacodynamic literature. HPLC quantitative analysis confirmed that the components timosaponin BⅡ and mangiferin were increased following ginger-processing, while 6-gingerol was identified as a unique component in GAR, a novel compound generated during ginger-processing. Molecular docking results indicated a strong binding affinity of these components with NF-kappaB and COX-2 proteins. CCK-8 assays demonstrated that at an LPS concentration of 1 microg/mL, mangiferin at 100 mumol/L, timosaponin BⅡ at 2 mumol/L, and 6-gingerol at 20 mumol/L, the cell viability exceeded 90%, with no significant cytotoxicity observed. ELISA results indicated that compared to the model group, the treatment groups treated with timosaponin BⅡ, mangiferin, and 6-gingerol significantly inhibited the release of TNF-alpha and IL-6 (P < 0.05). Furthermore, Western blot analysis confirmed that these compounds markedly upregulated the protein expression of IkappaBalpha while significantly downregulating the expression levels of NF-kappaB, p-NF-kappaB, nuclear NF-kappaB, and COX-2 (P < 0.05). This study demonstrates that GAR introduces 6-gingerol, a key anti-inflammatory component found in ginger, while also increasing the levels of mangiferin and timosaponin BⅡ. These differential components may enhance the anti-inflammatory efficacy of GAR by inhibiting the activation of the NF-kappaB signaling pathway and downregulating COX-2 protein expression, which in turn reduces the release of pro-inflammatory mediators such as IL-6 and TNF-alpha. By following the sequence of "component variation-enhanced efficacy-mechanism clarification," this study systematically elucidates the material basis, action mechanisms, and processing rationale that underlie the enhanced anti-inflammatory effects of GAR. Furthermore, it provides scientific support for the preservation of traditional processing techniques of GAR and its clinical applications.
abstract_zh: 本研究旨在分析知母(Anemarrhenae Rhizoma, AR)姜制前后化学成分差异，筛选关键差异性成分，并阐明其抗炎作用机制，进而明确炮制原理及姜制增效的科学内涵，为传统炮制技术的传承及姜制知母(Ginger-processed Anemarrhenae Rhizoma, GAR)的临床合理应用提供科学支撑。采用超高效液相色谱-四极杆-飞行时间-串联质谱(UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS)技术，在正、负离子模式下对AR和GAR中的化学成分进行定性分析。通过比较姜制前后成分含量的变化，以及新出现特征峰的识别，优先选择具有明确药理活性报道的新生成及含量上调的差异性成分作为目标化合物。随后采用高效液相色谱(HPLC)技术对关键差异性成分进行定量验证。进一步运用分子对接技术预测关键差异性成分与核因子kappa-B(NF-kappaB)及环氧合酶-2(COX-2)蛋白的结合能力。利用脂多糖(LPS)诱导的RAW264.7巨噬细胞建立炎症模型，通过CCK-8(Cell Counting Kit-8)实验确定关键差异性成分及LPS的最佳作用浓度。采用ELISA法检测细胞上清液中肿瘤坏死因子-alpha(TNF-alpha)和白细胞介素-6(IL-6)的水平，并通过Western blot(WB)技术检测IkappaBalpha、NF-kappaB、磷酸化NF-kappaB(p-NF-kappaB)、核内NF-kappaB及COX-2蛋白的表达水平。UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS分析在正、负离子模式下从AR和GAR中共鉴定出40个化合物，主要为皂苷类成分。基于姜制前后化学轮廓变化及药效文献，筛选出关键差异性成分（芒果苷、知母皂苷BⅡ、6-姜酚）。HPLC定量分析证实，姜制后知母皂苷BⅡ和芒果苷含量升高，而6-姜酚为GAR中特有成分，是姜制过程中新生成的化合物。分子对接结果显示，这些成分与NF-kappaB和COX-2蛋白具有较强的结合能力。CCK-8实验表明，在LPS浓度为1微克/毫升、芒果苷100微摩尔/升、知母皂苷BⅡ 2微摩尔/升、6-姜酚20微摩尔/升时，细胞存活率均超过90%，无明显细胞毒性。ELISA结果显示，与模型组相比，知母皂苷BⅡ、芒果苷和6-姜酚给药组均能显著抑制TNF-alpha和IL-6的释放(P < 0.05)。Western blot分析进一步证实，这些化合物显著上调IkappaBalpha蛋白表达，同时显著下调NF-kappaB、p-NF-kappaB、核内NF-kappaB及COX-2蛋白的表达水平(P < 0.05)。本研究证实，GAR引入了姜中关键抗炎成分6-姜酚，同时提高了芒果苷和知母皂苷BⅡ的含量。这些差异性成分可能通过抑制NF-kappaB信号通路激活及下调COX-2蛋白表达，减少IL-6和TNF-alpha等促炎介质的释放，从而增强GAR的抗炎疗效。本研究遵循“成分变化-增效作用-机制阐明”的研究思路，系统阐明了GAR抗炎增效的物质基础、作用机制及炮制原理，为GAR传统炮制技术的传承及其临床应用提供了科学依据。
